title: On-demand icons (e.g. Discover Notifier) can't be configured in the System Tray settings dialog until they become visible
line: The Updates entry is always listed in the System Tray settings, so it can be set to Always show or Never show even when there are no updates.
explanation: Since the fix for bug 413053, DiscoverNotifier created its StatusNotifierItem only when there was something to notify about and deleted it otherwise. With no item on D-Bus, the System Tray had no Updates entry to list in its settings, and "Always show" could not keep an icon that did not exist. The notifier now keeps the item registered and switches its status between Active and Passive (the Plasma 5 behaviour); the reboot menu actions are added when a reboot becomes needed instead of only at creation time.

commits.message:
notifier: keep the tray item registered when there is nothing to show

The status notifier item was deleted whenever there were no updates, so
the System Tray settings had no Updates entry to configure and "Always
show" did nothing. Keep the item around and switch it to Passive instead.

BUG: 495651

media.caption: No updates: searching "Updat" in System Tray Settings > Entries finds nothing (sweep tester, master).
No updates: the Updates entry is listed and configurable.
After updates went from 3 back to 0 the Updates entry vanished again (sweep tester, master).
After updates went from 3 back to 0 the entry stays, and with Always show the Updates icon stays in the panel.

review.text: Switching the SNI between Active and Passive instead of creating/deleting it is the standard SNI approach and the actual cause of the missing entry; Never show still removes it, which covers 413053's original wish. Moving the reboot menu actions into the needsRebootChanged handler is fine since that signal is emitted only once. It reverses a deliberate Discover choice, so the commit/MR text should mention 413053 so maintainers can weigh it.
